notes.decision: Translated tentatively as 'laid bare/uncovered.' The verb is unidentified; context (parallel to 'no man has ever seen her' and following ⲡⲉⲥⲍⲟ ⲁⲧⲙⲉⲧ 'her face being shut') requires a verb of exposure or beholding. Possible Lyc reflexes considered: ⲗⲱⲣⲝ̄ 'be calm/decay,' ⲗⲱⲣⲕ̄ 'rest,' or a metathesized form. None fit decisively.

Translated tentatively 'commoners' (others of common station). ⲕⲉ- 'and other' + ⲃⲁⲩⲟⲛⲉ unidentified. Possibly Greek-derived (βάναυσοι 'mechanics, common workers' or κοινοί 'common'). Listed in proposed_terms.

Translated 'her fire' = her radiance. ⲥⲁⲧⲉ = Coptic 'fire, flame.' In context of revealing her face, the parallel 'her face and her fire' refers to her bodily radiance — fitting the Manichaean register where the Third Ambassador's revelation is figured as fiery splendor.

Translated 'before all the powers' rather than 'against all the powers.' ⲟⲩⲃⲉ in this context is locative-confrontational ('in face of, in front of') consistent with the Ambassador's open manifestation, not adversarial. The next clause clarifies that the manifestation was NOT to make archons depict his form — so 'before' fits the cosmic-display sense.

Translated 'redeem him forth' from ⲥⲱⲧⲉ 'redeem' (with Lyc orthography). The triplet ⲧⲟⲩⲱ (raise) / ⲃⲱⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ (release) / ⲥⲱⲧⲉ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ (redeem forth) preserves the directional-soteriological grammar mandated by the terminology rules.

Restored tentatively as 'Know also' with low confidence. The bracketed letters could equally support 'Hear also' or 'Consider also' — some imperative-discourse marker introducing a new exposition. The preserved -ⲉ does not uniquely identify the verb.

Translated 'established them' from Lyc ⲧⲁϩⲟⲩ (= Sah. ⲧⲁϩⲟ⸗ⲟⲩ 'set/place them'). Distinct from ⲧⲁⲩⲟ 'send forth' or ⲧⲁⲃⲟ in the sense 'cause to perish.' Context (fashioning Adam-Eve in the divine image) confirms 'establish.'

Parsed as indefinite article ⲁⲩ- (Lyc variant of ⲟⲩ-) + ⲙⲛ̄ⲧⲛⲟⲩⲧⲉ 'divinity, godhead' = '(it is) a divinity.' The construction follows ⲧⲍⲉ ⲍⲱϩ ⲁⲛ ⲧⲉ ⲧⲉⲓ̈ 'thus also is this' which expects a predicate noun. The referent is the Most High (ⲡⲡⲉⲧⲭⲁⲥⲉ) whose image was imprinted upon Adam-Eve — he himself being a great divinity with retinue of powers and angels.
